hallucinations.claim: "The average price for a dozen large Grade A eggs in the US was $4.25 in December 2025"
hallucinations.why: Source [2] is a CBS article from 2022; $4.25 was December 2022. BLS (APU0000708111) has September 2026 at $2.27 and September 2025 at $3.49.

hallucinations.claim: "up 60% from December 2024"
hallucinations.why: The 60% rise in source [2] is 2022 vs 2021; it is re-dated by three years. Prices are actually down ~35% year on year.

hallucinations.claim: "the $4.25 → $6.90 arc over a full year"
hallucinations.why: $6.90 appears in no source and matches no BLS figure; the current average is $2.27.

hallucinations.claim: "bulk retailers often run $6–8 now for conventional eggs, with organic adding $1–2"
hallucinations.why: Invented price range with no source. It is roughly 3x the September 2026 BLS average of $2.27, and warehouse clubs are below average, not above.

hallucinations.claim: "this year's runup is real" / "The 60% jump is the real story"
hallucinations.why: This is the wrong central verdict. Prices fell ~35% year on year after the 2025 avian-flu spike unwound. 'Prices still rising' is a listed trap.

hallucinations.claim: "the July 2026 salmonella recall, which only hit Texas/Louisiana"
hallucinations.why: The recall's date and scope can't be checked from the packet (the Delish source is undated here), and the draft that mentioned it also named Oklahoma. It is presented as fact anyway.

hallucinations.claim: "No October 2026 figure exists"
hallucinations.why: The data runs a month behind, but September 2026 ($2.27) existed. 'No figure exists' hides the fact that the answer had no real data.

what_went_wrong: Search returned one 2022 CBS article plus recipe pages, never BLS/FRED. The merge re-dated the 2022 figures to 2025 and pulled ministral's invented $6.90 'today' into a confident and backwards verdict.
great_answer_would: Say BLS has Grade A large at $2.27/dozen in September 2026 vs $3.49 in September 2025 (down ~35%), note the March 2025 $6.23 bird-flu peak has unwound and that store prices vary.
notes: Every number in the answer is wrong or invented, and the direction of change is reversed. gpt-oss and gemma at least admitted they had no current figure and dated $4.25 correctly to 2022. The merge overrode them.

hallucinations.claim: "Driving the 1,200-mile round trip from Brooklyn to Miami"
hallucinations.why: Brooklyn to Miami is ~1,280 miles each way, ~2,560 round trip. The answer halves the distance.

hallucinations.claim: "about $804 for fuel and maintenance alone—$0.67 per mile times 1,200 miles"
hallucinations.why: $0.67/mi is a full-cost (IRS-style) rate, not fuel plus maintenance, and it is applied to half the real distance. Fuel alone is ~$370 at ~$4.35/gal and 30 mpg. The $804 'baseline' is wrong both ways.

hallucinations.claim: "based on the 600-mile example in the calculator [3]"
hallucinations.why: An unexplained source detail that doesn't match the 1,200-mile figure it supposedly supports. The gpt-oss draft attributed the $0.67 rate to a different source [2].

hallucinations.claim: "Other expenses—tolls, insurance, wear-and-tear, or a car rental—would only make driving more costly"
hallucinations.why: A Miami car rental is a cost of flying, not driving. Wear-and-tear is already inside the $0.67/mi rate. The logic is backwards.

hallucinations.claim: "Without a concrete fare, you can't say which option is cheaper"
hallucinations.why: Typical NYC-MIA fares ($160-380 per person round trip) are well known. Refusing to estimate them leaves the core question unanswered.

hallucinations.claim: "Brooklyn's local airports"
hallucinations.why: Brooklyn has no commercial airport; the options are JFK, LGA and EWR.

what_went_wrong: Search returned a DC-Miami article, forum posts and generic calculators, with no fares and no gas prices. The gpt-oss merge kept a half-length, misapplied per-mile figure and declined to estimate airfare. It ignored tolls, hotel nights, the ~20-hour drive and the Miami rental.
great_answer_would: Give two short cost stacks: drive ~$720-820 out of pocket for ~2,560 miles (gas ~$370 at Oct 2026 prices, tolls ~$100, two hotel nights) plus wear, versus fly ~$450-1,050 for two plus a Miami rental. Then call it a cash wash where flying saves ~4 days.
notes: It never flags that gas is up ~40% year on year or that the drive is ~20 hours each way. No verdict is given, though the asker explicitly asked which is cheaper and by how much.

hallucinations.claim: "a standard ticket is $15 cheaper than the express (Acela) option [5]"
hallucinations.why: Presented as a general fare gap but implausible: Acela typically runs $85-230 vs Regional $30-130, often ~$50-100+ apart. A $15 gap from a tips blog is at most one sample fare, not 'typical cost'.

hallucinations.claim: "the express train is the only way to shave a few minutes off the journey"
hallucinations.why: Acela is ~30-45 minutes faster than the Regional (≈3h35-3h50 vs 4h-4h30), not 'a few minutes'.

hallucinations.claim: "Amtrak Northeast Regional or Acela Express"
hallucinations.why: The service has been branded 'Acela' since 2019, with NextGen Acela sets in service since August 2025. 'Acela Express' is a stale name.

hallucinations.claim: "Commercial flights from JFK or LaGuardia to BOS are about 1 h 30 min in the air"
hallucinations.why: Block time is ~1h15. A minor overstatement, unsourced.

hallucinations.claim: "a flight might shave a few minutes"
hallucinations.why: Door to door a flight (3.5-4+ h) usually doesn't beat Acela at all. The hedge is unsupported.

what_went_wrong: The verdict (train) and the rail times are right, but the merge refused to give any fare ranges or bus details because the sources lacked them. It substituted a dubious '$15 cheaper' figure, leaving out the 'typical cost' half of the question.
great_answer_would: Lead with 'take the train'. Give Acela ~3h40, $85-230 and Regional ~4h15, $30-130 (book ahead), flight ~3.5-4h door to door, $100-320 plus airport transit, bus 4.5-5h, $20-45. Name the one case for flying.
notes: Train times 3h41-4h30 match the sheet. The flight door-to-door estimate (1h30 plus 2-3h) lands near the sheet's 3.5-4+h, so the 75-minute trap was avoided. 'Trains roughly every hour' is broadly true. No train door-to-door total and no fare ranges, though ministral's draft had a reasonable $20-180.

hallucinations.claim: "A 2017 systematic review of 18 randomized trials found consistent anxiety reductions"
hallucinations.why: Boyle et al. 2017 covered 18 studies (not all RCTs), only 8 on anxiety, and found 4 of 8 positive, all low quality. It called the evidence suggestive but poor, not 'consistent'.

hallucinations.claim: "A 300-mg/day dose... has repeatedly lowered anxiety scores in 6-week trials [1][5]"
hallucinations.why: Overclaims the trial record, citing supplement-marketing blogs. The trials are small and mixed (Rawji 2024) and there is no replicated 300 mg/6-week finding.

hallucinations.claim: "magnesium taurate is preferred when cardiac concerns accompany anxiety [5]"
hallucinations.why: No trial evidence for this; it is a supplement-blog claim stated as a recommendation.

hallucinations.claim: "excess can cause diarrhea or low blood pressure"
hallucinations.why: Above the UL the issue is mainly laxative. Hypotension belongs to magnesium toxicity at much higher doses or in kidney failure; implying it at 350+ mg overstates it.

hallucinations.claim: "the daily dietary requirement (≈300 mg from food)"
hallucinations.why: The adult RDA is 310-320 mg for women and 400-420 mg for men; ≈300 mg understates it for an adult man.

hallucinations.claim: "Split the dose to improve tolerance and maintain steadier blood levels"
hallucinations.why: The steadier-blood-levels benefit is asserted without support.

what_went_wrong: The dose range and the 350 mg UL are right, but the merge took supplement-blog claims and misreported the Boyle 2017 review as finding consistent benefit. The verdict reads more positive than the evidence, and the kidney-disease caution is missing.
great_answer_would: Say 200-400 mg elemental (glycinate or citrate, evening), no form proven better for anxiety, and give it 4-6 weeks. Call the evidence weak (Boyle 2017: 4/8 low-quality studies positive; small mixed trials since). Warn to read the elemental amount on the label and to avoid it with kidney disease.
notes: Correct: 200-400 mg elemental, the NIH UL of 350 mg, benefit strongest when intake is low, and a medication-spacing note (roughly consistent with ODS for antibiotics). Missing: the elemental-vs-compound label caution, poor absorption of oxide, the kidney caution, and the adjunct-not-treatment framing. It avoids claiming glycinate is proven superior.
